hyp-2.note: title: 'CFH deficiency ... exacerbating glomerular injury' (loss of CFH worsens disease, so neg). The title reads as severity, but the chain's last step says the pathway leads_to IgA nephropathy, so the claim takes the chain's aspect, risk. hyp-3.no_claim_reason: the title says the three genes 'modulate' mucosal innate immunity, the mechanism says 'alterations' in these defences trigger aberrant responses, and the falsification expects 'unknown': no direction for any gene's overall effect on IgA nephropathy, although each chain step is signed positive

findings.detail: every intermediate node ('B cell', 'IgA', 'complement alternative pathway', 'innate immune response') is left as kind 'other' with no CURIE, although CL:0000236, GO:0071745, GO:0006957 and GO:0045087 exist.
neither cited text mentions B cells: UniProt TNFSF13 gives TACI/BCMA binding, tumour cell growth and monocyte/macrophage processes; the ChEMBL record gives atacicept as a TNFSF13 inhibitor.

the MGI record (Tnfsf13 knockout mice have decreased IgA) states TNFSF13 raises IgA directly in mouse, which is the hypothesis title, but the run filed it under the B cell step, which it does not state; B cells appear in no cited text.
'IgA leads to IgA nephropathy' is cited to a ChEMBL drug indication (atacicept, phase 3 for IgAN) and a GWAS row for rs3803800-A; neither names IgA as a cause.

the cited ChEMBL record itself says atacicept is a decoy receptor for both TNFSF13 (APRIL) and TNFSF13B (BAFF), and the indication record gives only the phase reached, not efficacy, so neither isolates a TNFSF13 effect on IgA nephropathy.
confidence 'high', yet none of its five citations states the step it is cited for; every step of its chain has empty evidence.

confidence 'high', yet only the first step (CFH inhibits the alternative pathway, UniProt) is supported; the disease step rests on a mouse Cfh-knockout glomerulonephritis annotation (gene not pathway, parent disease) and a CFH-locus GWAS row.
all three hypotheses set support 'speculative' while confidence is 'high', 'high' and 'medium': the run's two self-assessments disagree.

'complement alternative pathway leads to IgAN' is cited to Cfh knockout mice with glomerulonephritis (a gene, and the parent disease) and to rs6677604-G (a CFH-locus association); no text names the pathway as a cause of IgAN.

title and mechanism describe CFH deficiency as aggravating glomerular injury within IgAN (severity), and the falsification reads out glomerular damage, but the chain's last step says the pathway leads_to IgAN (cause, risk).

the mechanism invokes 'genetic variants that reduce CFH function', but the cited rs6677604 row gives only the G allele's OR 1.21 for IgAN, with no statement of what the allele does to CFH; the variant's direction is never connected to CFH function.

every chain step is signed positive (more CARD9/ITGAX/DEFA4 activity, more innate immunity, more IgAN), but the title says 'modulate', the mechanism 'alterations ... disrupt intestinal homeostasis' (which reads more like loss of defence causing disease) and the falsification expects 'unknown'; the chain commits to a sign the hypothesis does not.

steps 1 to 3 are parallel (each gene to innate immune response) and do connect through step 4, but the title's 'pathogenic IgA production' and 'intestinal defense' are absent, so the chain jumps from innate immune response straight to IgAN, while the falsification reads out IgA, a node the chain never reaches.

ITGAX UniProt text gives fibrinogen receptor, cell-cell interaction during inflammatory responses, monocyte adhesion and chemotaxis; the MGI record gives impaired hematopoiesis; neither names the innate immune response.
DEFA4 UniProt text describes an antimicrobial host-defense peptide (an effector), not something that activates the innate immune response; it is the step's only citation.

'innate immune response leads to IgAN' is cited to a STRING publication enrichment (a paper title) and three variant association rows; the only text linking immunity against intestinal pathogens to IgAN is that paper title, seen through an enrichment.

rs2738058 is intergenic, its author-reported gene is 'DEFA' (the cluster), its closest genes are DEFA9P/DEFA10P and DEFA4 is 25.8 kb away and not closest; rs7190997's author-reported gene is 'ITGAX-ITGAM'; the run treats them as DEFA4 and ITGAX evidence.

the five GWAS rows give signed allele associations with IgAN (rs3803800-A OR 1.21 in TNFSF13, rs6677604-G OR 1.21 in CFH, rs4077515-T OR 1.14 in CARD9, rs7190997-C OR 1.223, rs2738058-T OR 1.267), but no chain has a variant node, so the run's only human genetic evidence is cited for process-to-disease steps it cannot state.
the mechanism names poorly O-glycosylated IgA1 as the pathogenic species, but the chain node is plain 'IgA' and the only IgA-level citation is total IgA in mouse.
every hypothesis has empty supporting_evidence and contradicting_evidence lists; the run judged no contradicting citations.

the abstention for OR4X1 and ZNF174 cites 'GWAS:OR4X1:no-association', 'CHEMBL:no-target-OR4X1', 'STRING:no-edges' and similar ids that are not in sources.json, so its 'grounded' support cannot be checked; it also reads absence of records as 'unrelated to the disease'.

a cell type as an effect target ('TNFSF13 activates B cell'): there is no cellType target kind, so 'B cell' was grounded as the process GO:0042113 B cell activation at both ends, which keeps the run's own link between the two steps.

'IgA' is exactly GO:0071745 IgA immunoglobulin complex, a component, which cannot be an amount target; grounded instead as PR:000050176 IgA heavy chain protein (both subclasses, any species), the protein that defines the isotype, as the sibling run single_agent-r3 did.

a cited text that states a shortcut of the chain (MGI: Tnfsf13 knockout lowers IgA, i.e. TNFSF13 raises IgA) has no home: it states no run step, and a bridge is allowed only when an arm needs it to compose, which this arm does not; the run's best mechanistic citation for hyp-1 is therefore excluded.

a hypothesis whose chain is fully signed but whose title and mechanism give no direction gets no_claim_reason, so the three signed gene-to-IgAN routes are never composed; a claim 'sign from the chain, unconfirmed by the title' would let them be tested.
the run's abstention (two genes declined with cited reasons) has no place in curated.json, so it can only be recorded as a finding.

the guide says the claim targets 'the disease the chain concludes' but not whose aspect wins when the title (exacerbating, severity) and the chain's last step (leads_to, risk) disagree; the chain's was used.

S4 and S6 each reach 'established' (b = 4/5, exactly the 0.8 threshold) on a single UniProt function sentence; for S6 that sentence only says CARD9 'plays a key role in' the antifungal innate immune response, so one database summary line is enough to establish a statement.
